faq.title: Guides & FAQ
faq.subtitle: Step-by-step guides and answers to common questions about FluxerList.
faq.guides.botSubmission.title: Bot Submission Guide
faq.guides.botSubmission.description: Requirements, review stages, privacy disclosures, and tips to get approved faster.
faq.guides.markdownReference.title: Markdown Reference
faq.guides.markdownReference.description: All supported formatting syntax for server, bot, and theme descriptions - headings, lists, code blocks, highlights, and more.
faq.guides.rssAtom.title: RSS & Atom Feed Guide
faq.guides.rssAtom.description: Subscribe to new server listings in any feed reader, filter by category, or pull fresh listings into your own apps and automations.
faq.a.whatIsNew: Shows servers in the order they were added to FluxerList, with the most recently listed servers first.
faq.a.whatIsMembers: Sorts servers by their member count from largest to smallest, so the biggest communities appear at the top.
faq.a.whatIsPopular: Sorts servers by the total number of votes they have received - the more votes, the higher the ranking.
faq.a.howDoCategories: Categories filter servers by their tags. When you select a category like Gaming or Music, only servers that have that tag will be shown.
faq.a.canISearch: Yes - the search bar matches against server names, descriptions, and tags simultaneously.
faq.q.howAddServer: How do I add my server?
faq.a.howAddServer: Log in with your Fluxer account, then click Add Server. Fill in your server details and submit - your listing will be reviewed before it goes live.
faq.a.howLongApproval: Most servers are reviewed within 24-48 hours. You can track your submission status on your profile dashboard.
faq.a.whyRejected: Common reasons include an invalid invite link, a description that violates our guidelines, or missing required information. Check your dashboard for any notes from reviewers.
faq.q.canIEdit: Can I edit my server after submitting?
faq.a.canIEdit: Yes - go to your profile dashboard, find your server, and click the Edit button to update the description, tags, invite link, and more.
faq.q.howDelete: How do I delete my server listing?
faq.a.howDelete: Go to your profile dashboard, find the server, and click Delete. You will be asked to confirm before it is permanently removed.
faq.q.howSubmitBot: How do I submit a bot?
faq.a.howSubmitBot: Log in with Fluxer, then go to Submit a Bot. Read the Bot Submission Guide first - it explains everything reviewers check.
faq.q.howLongBotReview: How long does bot review take?
faq.a.howLongBotReview: Bot reviews typically take 2-5 days. They're more thorough than server reviews - we add your bot to a private test community and verify every command.
faq.a.whyBotRejected: Common reasons: mismatched permissions, an invalid invite URL, missing privacy disclosures, or commands not responding within the expected time. Check your dashboard for reviewer notes.
faq.q.howManyBots: How many bots can I submit?
faq.a.howManyBots: Up to 5 bots per account. If you need to list more, reach out in the support server.
faq.q.botCriteria: Where can I read the full bot review criteria?
faq.a.botCriteria: The Bot Submission Guide covers all requirements, the 5-stage review process, privacy rules, and tips to get approved faster.
faq.a.whatIsBumping: Bumping refreshes your server's position in the listings and signals activity. You can bump each server once every 12 hours.
faq.q.howToVote: How do I vote for a server?
faq.a.howToVote: Open any server's page and click the Vote button. You need to be logged in with your Fluxer account to vote.
faq.a.howOftenVote: You can vote for each server once. If you change your mind, you can remove your vote at any time.
faq.a.howLogin: FluxerList uses Fluxer OAuth - click Login and you will be taken to Fluxer to authorise. No separate account is needed.
faq.a.emailCollect: No. FluxerList only requests your Fluxer username, display name, and avatar. We do not request or store your email address.
faq.q.affiliated: Is FluxerList officially affiliated with Fluxer?
faq.a.affiliated: No. FluxerList is an independent, community-run project and is not officially affiliated with or endorsed by Fluxer Platform AB.
faq.q.getHelp: Where can I get help or report an issue?
faq.a.getHelp: Join our FluxerList community server - our team and community members are on hand to help.
faq.q.reportServer: How do I report a server that violates the rules?
faq.a.reportServer: Please report it in our community server and a moderator will review it.
faq.stillHaveQuestionsDesc: Our team and community are in the support server and happy to help.

flat.hero.title: FLAT
flat.hero.subtitle: Fluxer List Activity Tracking
flat.hero.description: A transparent, real-time scoring system that measures how alive and engaged a Fluxer community is, based on real behaviour, not just vote counts.
flat.what.heading: A score that reflects how alive your community really is
flat.what.p1: FLAT produces a single number that captures a community's activity level. It combines signals from messages, voice sessions, new joins, and bumps, each weighted by how much they indicate genuine engagement.
flat.what.p2: Scores update every hour and decay over time. A server that was busy last month but has gone quiet will see its score drop naturally. A server whose community picks back up will see it climb again.
flat.what.noContent: No message content is ever read or stored.
flat.what.countsOnly: FLAT only ever sees counts, never what was said.
flat.signals.heading: What we track
flat.signals.subtitle: Seven signals feed into the FLAT score. Each one is a count, never content.
flat.signals.messages.name: Messages sent
flat.signals.messages.description: Total messages posted across all channels. Content is never read.
flat.signals.reactions.name: Reactions added
flat.signals.reactions.description: Emoji reactions on messages, a lightweight signal of engagement.
flat.signals.voice.name: Voice time
flat.signals.voice.description: Aggregate minutes spent in voice channels across all members.
flat.signals.commands.name: Bot commands
flat.signals.commands.description: Members using bot commands show the community is actively engaging with its tools.
flat.signals.joins.name: Members joining
flat.signals.joins.description: New member joins show real community growth and attraction.
flat.signals.leaves.name: Members leaving
flat.signals.leaves.description: Members leaving applies a small penalty — sustained churn signals a less healthy community.
flat.signals.bumps.name: FluxerList bumps
flat.signals.bumps.description: Bumping your server on FluxerList shows active owner engagement.
flat.calc.heading: How the score is calculated
flat.calc.weighted.title: Weighted signals
flat.calc.weighted.description: Not all activity is equal. Joining a server is a stronger signal of growth than adding a single emoji reaction, so it earns more points. The weights are fixed and public, shown in the table below.
flat.calc.decay.title: Time decay
flat.calc.decay.description: Recent activity matters more than old activity. Points earned today count fully; points from last week count for a fraction. A server that was busy months ago but has gone quiet will see its score drop naturally over time.
flat.calc.table.heading: Signal weights
flat.calc.note: Scores are recalculated and published every hour. The last update time is shown on each server's listing.
flat.privacy.heading: Privacy first, by design
flat.privacy.subtitle: FLAT was built to be as unintrusive as possible. Here is exactly what we do and don't do  with activity data.
flat.privacy.p1: No user IDs are ever stored. All tracking is aggregated at the server level.
flat.privacy.p2: Message content is never read, stored, or transmitted. Only counts are recorded.
flat.privacy.p3: Only server-level aggregates (totals, not per-user breakdowns) are processed.
flat.privacy.p4: Servers can opt out at any time. Toggle tracking off in your server dashboard.
flat.privacy.p5: Activity data is retained for 90 days by default, then automatically purged.
flat.tiers.heading: FLAT score tiers
flat.tiers.subtitle: Your FLAT score determines which tier badge appears on your listing. Tiers update in real time as your score changes.
flat.tiers.thriving.name: Thriving
flat.tiers.thriving.description: A vibrant, highly active community with strong daily engagement.
flat.tiers.active.name: Active
flat.tiers.active.description: Regular activity with a solid base of engaged members.
flat.tiers.moderate.name: Moderate
flat.tiers.moderate.description: Some consistent activity, but with clear room to grow.
flat.tiers.quiet.name: Quiet
flat.tiers.quiet.description: Low recent activity. Score will rise again as the community picks up.
flat.faq.heading: Common questions
flat.faq.q1: Can server owners game the FLAT score?
flat.faq.a1: We have protections in place to prevent this. Every signal type has a per-hour cap, so flooding a channel with messages won't produce an outsized score. Scores also decay naturally. Any artificial spike fades within 24–48 hours without sustained real activity to back it up.
flat.faq.q2: Why is my score lower than I expected?
flat.faq.a2: FLAT applies time decay, so recent activity carries more weight than older activity. If your server had a busy period a while ago but has been quieter recently, the score will reflect that current reality. Encourage members to stay active and the score will climb again.
flat.faq.q3: How do I see my server's FLAT data?
flat.faq.a3: Detailed per-signal breakdowns are available in your server dashboard. Navigate to your server's management page to see a live breakdown of each signal contributing to your current score.
flat.faq.q4: Can I opt out of FLAT tracking?
flat.faq.a4: Yes. Any server owner can disable FLAT tracking from the server settings in their dashboard. Opting out means the server won't appear in activity-sorted listings, but it will still be discoverable via search and category filters.
flat.cta.heading: Ready to see your score?
flat.cta.description: Browse servers sorted by FLAT score, or head to your dashboard to see a detailed breakdown for your own server.
